acceptance: internal/landed judges a commit's tree as well as a worktree, and its commit-tree mode has its own red-first tests, including a checkpoint full-tree commit
wtcheckpoint.hasLanded calls landed.Changes and keeps no path-by-path landed walk of its own
The decision to keep or loosen the prune's exact-equality rule is recorded in docs/architecture/packages/internal-landed.md with the test that pins it
fix: Two separately reviewed components. (1) Give internal/landed a commit-tree mode: judge a commit's tree against its merge-base with origin/main, red first, including a checkpoint pair (staged commit on HEAD, full tree on that). (2) Make wtcheckpoint.hasLanded call landed.Changes on the checkpoint's full-tree commit, deleting its own path walk. Whether the prune may loosen from exact equality to the merge proof is its own reviewed decision, because the prune deletes a ref: if kept strict, pass a strictness option rather than keep a second implementation.
source: console lane cl-gc, rebase onto train #780 (evolve checkpoint) and the GC architecture re-review, 2026-10-06
summary: Two proofs answer whether work already landed in origin/main. internal/landed (Changes, Untracked) judges a worktree path by path through a three-way git merge-file, and evolve worktree cleanup --dev removes a dev tree on it. wtcheckpoint.hasLanded (go/internal/wtcheckpoint/prune.go) judges a checkpoint commit by exact equality of its changed paths with main, and evolve checkpoint prune --landed deletes refs/checkpoints/* on it. Both name the ref through plane.OriginMainRef, but the proof logic is duplicated and can drift. internal/landed judges worktrees only: its commit-tree mode was removed in review because nothing called it.
title: evolve checkpoint prune --landed keeps its own equality-only landed check beside internal/landed
